chunks: And by his chain, he said:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) disliked entering a dark house except with a lantern.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet dislike regarding entering a dark house?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to highlight the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practical wisdom in avoiding the fear (*khauf*) associated with darkness, linking physical visibility to spiritual and psychological comfort. This specific prohibition underscores the broader Shia emphasis on removing causes of anxiety and ensuring safety in daily conduct, reflecting the Prophet’s meticulous attention to both the physical and emotional well-being of the community.

en.hubeali: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> disliked entering a dark house except with a lantern’.
en.sarwar: 6. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith
the following is narrated: “The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, disliked entering a dark house without a lamp.”
